extension.summary: Flexible IPTV for Xtream Codes and M3U sources
Flexibele IPTV voor Xtream Codes en M3U-bronnen
extension.description: Reads your channel list from the Xtream API instead of a bulk get.php download, so it keeps working on providers where IPTV Simple fails. Writes a clean local M3U for IPTV Simple to read, so you keep Kodi's native EPG grid, and browses movies and series in the add-on itself. Includes diagnostics that report exactly what your provider accepts and refuses.

Haalt je kanaallijst uit de Xtream API in plaats van uit een grote get.php-download, en blijft daardoor werken bij providers waar IPTV Simple faalt. Schrijft een schone lokale M3U die IPTV Simple inleest, zodat je Kodi's eigen programmagids houdt, en bladert films en series in de add-on zelf. Bevat diagnostiek die precies laat zien wat je provider accepteert en weigert.
extension.news: 0.3.0 - Add a companion .nfo next to every movie/episode's .strm file, self-contained (title/plot/year/genre/rating/poster from the provider itself, no online scraper match needed) and tagged with the provider's own "LAND | Source" category (Netflix, Videoland, Bioscoop, ...). Kodi's library view can filter/browse by Tag the same way it does Genre, bringing back quick per-source browsing for series too (lost in 0.2.5 when the source folder had to be removed there) without depending on folder structure. Also fixes titles silently missing from the library because TMDB couldn't match a decorated filename ("Aquaman and the Lost Kingdom 4K (NL) (851703)") - there is nothing left to match now. 0.2.5 - Fix series still not appearing in Kodi despite syncing correctly (2 shows visible out of 2389): the per-source folder introduced in 0.2.2 broke Kodi's TV scanner, which expects exactly one level of nesting (TV root/Show/episodes) and does not look inside an intermediate folder it fails to recognize as a show - confirmed in the log, Kodi reported "No information found" for the *source* folder itself and never descended into the real show folders beneath it. Movies keep their source folder (confirmed working, Kodi's movie scanner is not as strict); episodes now sit directly under their show folder with no source folder above it. 0.2.4 - Fix the automatic post-sync library scan not actually working (a manual "Update library" in Kodi's own UI was required): the raw VideoLibrary.Scan JSON-RPC call reported success but its scan aborted after a single item, likely a race with Kodi's own directory cache right after tens of thousands of files were just written. Now triggers the scan the same way Kodi's own "Update library" menu item does (UpdateLibrary), confirmed matching the working manual behaviour. 0.2.3 - Fix 0.2.2 not being enough: real show names (not just contrived worst cases) were still overflowing the path-length budget, because the show name was repeated three times over (the folder, the filename prefix, and again inside the provider's own doubled title). Episode filenames no longer repeat the show name - Kodi already gets that from the parent folder - which is what actually fixes real series instead of just reducing how often the problem shows up. 0.2.2 - Fix the library sync crashing on series: one provider returns an episode title that already contains "Show - S01E02 - Real Title", and doubled against this add-on's own naming that could exceed Windows' path length limit and silently abort the whole sync after only a couple of shows (surfacing as Kodi's generic "Something went wrong"). Filenames are now kept within a safe length, and one bad title can no longer take the rest of the catalogue down with it - it's skipped and logged instead. Also: .strm files are now organized by the provider's own "NL | Source" category (Netflix, Videoland, ...) as a folder per source, matching its own structure, instead of one flat pile. 0.2.1 - Keep the library sync from 0.2.0 up to date automatically: service.py now reruns it on the same schedule as the channel export, and triggers Kodi's own library scan afterwards (via JSON-RPC, in-process, no webserver needed) so new or removed movies/episodes actually show up without any manual steps. New settings: Library > "Keep the Kodi library in sync" and the country prefix to use (default NL). 0.2.0 - Add a "Sync NL movies & series to Kodi library" menu action: writes .strm files into local folders, since pointing a Kodi video source directly at the add-on (0.1.9) turned out unreliable - Kodi accepted the content-type setting but never actually scanned it (confirmed: the add-on was never invoked). See "Show paths" for the folder locations to add as ordinary Kodi sources. 0.1.9 - Add an optional country filter to category browsing (?country=NL), so Movies/TV Shows can be added as a Kodi video library source that only ever lists categories starting with a given country code instead of every category the provider has. 0.1.8 - Replace the ffmpegdirect reconnect approach (0.1.6/0.1.7) with a local proxy: the provider's actual failure mode is a hard HTTP error on the very first request, not a dropped connection, and ffmpeg's reconnect_on_http_error option (the one that would cover that) turns out not to be forwarded by the installed inputstream.ffmpegdirect build at all - no Kodi property could ever have reached it. Movies and episodes now play through a small local HTTP server (in service.py) that makes the real, retried request before Kodi ever sees a response, including on seeks. 0.1.7 - Fix 0.1.6 not actually working: ffmpegdirect was correctly configured with reconnect options, but left at its default "open mode" it silently routes plain http(s) VOD I/O back through Kodi's own cURL (confirmed via its own debug log: "IO handled by Kodi's cURL"), the exact code path 0.1.6 was trying to get away from — so the reconnect options were simply never used. 0.1.6 - Fix intermittent VOD/live playback failures at the root cause instead of papering over them: Kodi's native player retries a failed connection only once, 35ms later, which cannot ride out the provider's brief backend hiccups. Movies and episodes (not just live TV) now play through inputstream.ffmpegdirect with ffmpeg's real HTTP reconnect enabled, the same class of resilience a player like TiviMate has natively. The pre-flight probe added in 0.1.3/0.1.5 is removed: it added a wait before playback without a reliability guarantee. 0.1.5 - Re-add the 0.1.3 playback probe, reverted in 0.1.4, after further testing showed the "competing connection" theory behind the revert did not hold up. 0.1.4 - Revert 0.1.3: the playback probe appeared to compete with Kodi's own connection. 0.1.3 - Probe the resolved URL before handing it to Kodi, to absorb transient provider 502s. 0.1.2 - Fix live TV playback failures ("Error creating demuxer"): the exported User-Agent was being silently truncated at its first space by IPTV Simple's own M3U parser, so the provider saw an incomplete header and refused the connection. The value is now quoted in the export. 0.1.1 - Fix VOD playback (ffmpegdirect was wrongly forced into live/timeshift mode for movies and episodes) and missing posters/thumbnails (artwork URLs now carry the provider's required User-Agent header). 0.1.0 - First release: Xtream API browsing, M3U export for IPTV Simple, VOD and series, provider diagnostics.
